subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group-chat isolation be solved with sender-scoped sessions and memory namespaces, automatic per-user group subagents, or a Feishu plugin experiment before any core or SDK contract is added?
rationale: The request crosses cross-user memory, skills, config, admin, lifecycle, quota, and message-routing boundaries that automation cannot safely choose from source evidence alone.

options.title: Design The Feishu Isolation Seam First
options.body: Use current sender/topic session and subagent binding primitives as inputs, define memory/config/lifecycle/security boundaries, and implement only the approved seam.

options.title: Prototype In The Feishu Plugin
options.body: Validate routing, cleanup, quotas, shared/private memory, and admin controls inside the Feishu plugin before promoting any SDK or core contract.

options.title: Defer Heavy Group Subagents
options.body: Keep narrower session-routing, threading, and skill-preference issues open while avoiding automatic group subagent orchestration for now.

recommendation.title: Design The Feishu Isolation Seam First
recommendation.body: Use current sender/topic session and subagent binding primitives as inputs, define memory/config/lifecycle/security boundaries, and implement only the approved seam.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily Feishu channel behavior and plugin-boundary design, and repository metadata names m1heng as the Feishu community maintainer.
